headline: Recommended bonds of up to $3,000,000 for Nashua Public Library renovation design.
summary: Residents spoke during public comment in support of a library staff collective bargaining agreement. The board recommended bonds not to exceed $3,000,000 for design and ancillary costs to renovate the library. It also approved paying September 2026 library bills, using up to $7,500 from the Bloomfield Trust for half the fee of a 2027 author visit, and giving the director authority to dispose of a kiosk.
decisions: Approved payment of September 2026 library bills: $31,867.04 from the regular budget and $51.29 from the Fines account, 7-0.
Approved using up to $7,500 from the Bloomfield Trust to pay half the fee for the 2027 Nashua Reads author visit, 7-0.
Approved the minutes of the September 1, 2026 meeting, 7-0.
Recommended approval of bonds not to exceed $3,000,000 for design and ancillary costs to renovate the Nashua Public Library, 7-0.
Recommended giving some deaccessioned library items to the Friends of the Nashua Library for its annual booksale.
Approved giving Director McCormack authority to de-accession a kiosk bought with Burbank trust funds, 7-0.

plain_text:
Nashua Public Library Board of Trustees  
October 6, 2026  
7:00 PM  
MINUTES 
A meeting of the Nashua Public Library Board of Trustees was held Tuesday, October 6, 2026, scheduled 
at 7:00 PM at the Nashua Public Library, 2 Court Street, Nashua, NH, 03060  
1. Call to Order 
 
  
 
DRAFT 
 
 
Chairman Laflamme called the meeting to order at 7:07 PM.  
2. Attendance 
 
 Present: Linda Laflamme, Kristin Kane, Scott Jaquith, John Kennedy, Patricia Dresner, Ernest 
Jette, Padmaja Kunapareddy, Library Director Jennifer McCormack, Assistant Library Director Jenn 
Hosking. 
 
Forty five members of the public. 
3. Communications 
 
  
4. Public Comment 
 
 Motion by Ms. Kane, seconded by Mr. Jaquith, to extend the public comment period, not to exceed 
45 minutes. 
 
Vote: Yes, 7, No, 0 
Motion: PASSED 
 
Tracy Kittredge, Lori Silva, Mary Ellen Gilson, Erin Koehler, Faith Eherts, Ben Heney, Charles 
Ivanow, Eve Arnold, Jon Blanchette, Gary Hoffman, David Vorbach, Bill McIntyre, Tanya Prather, 
Ray Jackson, Bob Keating all expressed support for a library staff collective bargaining agreement.  
5. Approval of bills and trust fund requests 
 
 Motion by Mr. Jaquith, seconded by Mr. Kennedy to approve payment of the library bills from 
September 2026 from the regular budget for $31,867.04 and $51.29 from the Fines account. 
 
Vote: Yes, 7, No 0 
Motion: PASSED 
 
Motion by Mr. Jaquith, seconded by Ms. Kunapareddy to expend up to $7,500 from the Bloomfield 
Trust to fund half the fee for the 2027 Nashua Reads author visit. 
 
Vote: Yes, 7, No 0 
Motion: PASSED 
6. Approval of minutes from previous meeting 
 
 Motion by Ms. Kane, seconded by Ms. Dresner, to approve the September 1, 2026 meeting
minutes. 
 
Vote: Yes, 7, No 0 
Motion: PASSED 
7. Recommendation of R-26-027 related to bond for next phase of design 
 
 Motion by Mr. Kennedy, seconded by Ms. Kunapareddy, to recommend approval of R-26-067, 
authorizing the Mayor and City Treasurer to issue bonds not to exceed $3,000,000 for the design 
and ancillary costs to renovate the Nashua Public Library. 
 
Vote: Yes, 7, No, 0 
Motion: PASSED 
8. Request to deaccession certain items  
 
 Director McCormack requested to de-accession some items from the library's storage. The Board 
recommended some items be given to the Friends of the Nashua Library to include in their annual 
booksale. 
 
Motion made by Mr. Kennedy, seconded by Ms. Dresner, to give Director McCormack authority to 
de-accession a kiosk purchased using Burbank trust funds by first offering it to local organizations 
and then disposing of if there are no interested parties. 
 
Vote: Yes, 7, No, 0 
Motion: PASSED 
9. Renovation project update 
 
 Director McCormack discussed her recent visit to other recently renovated libraries and shared a 
discussion regarding possible sustainability features for the new building design.   
10. Approval of Director travel 
 
 Director McCormack shared plans to visit three libraries highlighted in Library Journal's "Design 
Showcase" located out of state. The Board expressed support for this travel.  
11. New Business 
 
 None. 
12. Adjourn 
 
 Motion by Mr. Jaquith, seconded by Mr. Kennedy, to adjourn the meeting at 8:39 PM. 
 
Vote: Yes, 7, No, 0 
Motion: PASSED
